{"decision":"**RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.** Anthony, 2026-09-14.

═══ THE IDEA, in his words ═══

"In the storyflow project (you can ssh to the other machine and look for the 2 pass extraction process), but this would maybe be similar in that you would have a schema (with all the SE terms defined up-front) that tell the agent how to parse a user provided description. It could be done at /genesis or /adopt, but might be good when the agent is looking is given any design related prompt to help it extract the content in a systematic extraction manner."

═══ WHAT IS ACTUALLY BEING PROPOSED ═══

Not new vocabulary — a new **ORDER OF OPERATIONS**. Today extraction is one pass: the agent reads the user's words and produces nodes, with its own judgement doing the routing in flight. Two-pass means the SE terms are laid out first, as a schema the parse is performed AGAINST, and only then is the description read. The claim is that a parse against a stated schema is more systematic — and, crucially, more REVIEWABLE — than a parse against an agent's priors.

**⭐ THE REASON THIS IS NOT THE SAME AS `describe_schema`**: the vocabulary is already served on demand. What is proposed is that it be CONSULTED AS A FIRST STEP rather than available as a lookup. That is a behavioural claim, not a content one, and it is the same distinction `dec:idea-does-the-black-box-frame-reach-the-agent-at-call-time` drew when it found the frame stated nowhere the agent reads at call time.

═══ THE SECOND QUESTION, AND IT MAY BE THE HARDER ONE: WHEN ═══

Anthony offers three answers and does not choose:

- **At `/genesis` or `/adopt`** — once, at the start. Cheap; nothing recurring. ⚠️ But Alex's failure was not at genesis; it arrived mid-project, on a word nobody had needed before.
- **On any design-related prompt** — every capture parses against the schema. Most thorough. ⚠️ And it is a cost on every single capture, paid to serve the ambiguous minority — the exact objection recorded against option (b) of `dec:idea-a-users-domain-vocabulary-has-no-route-into-se-vocabulary`.
- **On ambiguity only** — implied rather than stated, and it is the same trigger the follow-on question set in `dec:idea-the-interviews-answers-become-the-projects-own-se-reference` would use.

═══ ⚠️ THE REFERENCE HAS NOT BEEN READ ═══

storyflow's two-pass extraction lives on the LAN peer (ajs77, `~/projects/`) and **nobody has looked at it for this purpose**. Everything above is inference from one sentence describing it. What it actually does, what the two passes actually are, and whether the analogy holds are all unchecked — and this project has a standing lesson about exactly this shape (`fact:dev-storyflow-feedback...`: a file's identity and age are read off the FILE, never off a note about it). **Reading it is the cheapest thing that would make this decidable**, and it has not been done.

═══ OPTIONS, none chosen ═══

**(a) NOTHING. One-pass extraction with a routing table is what shipped, and it works for most captures.** ⚠️ Counter: it demonstrably did not work for Alex, and its failure mode is silent — a confident wrong category, not an error.

**(b) SCHEMA-FIRST AT GENESIS AND ADOPT ONLY.** Cheapest real change; fits where the interview already runs. ⚠️ Counter: misses the mid-project arrival, which is when it actually broke.

**(c) SCHEMA-FIRST ON EVERY DESIGN PROMPT.** ⚠️ Counter: pays on every capture for the ambiguous minority, and reflow2's own recorded objection to that pattern is on file.

**(d) SCHEMA-FIRST ONLY ON AMBIGUITY**, sharing a trigger with the follow-on interview questions. ⚠️ Counter: requires the agent to DETECT its own ambiguity, which is the part nothing has ever demonstrated — Alex's agent did not notice it was unsure, it noticed it was stuck and asked him. Detecting "I have two defensible readings" is a harder problem than either pass.

═══ WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS DECIDABLE ═══

Two things, both cheap and neither done: **read storyflow's two-pass extraction** rather than reasoning from a description of it; and establish whether an agent can reliably tell "ambiguous" from "clear", because options (d) and the whole follow-on-questions idea rest on it.","kind":"exploratory","name":"OPEN — should extraction be TWO-PASS against an SE schema stated up front, the way storyflow parses, and does it run at genesis/adopt or on every design prompt?","rationale":"Recorded as an open question via the brainstorm discipline, and deliberately NOT researched before recording — the reference on the LAN peer is named as unread rather than summarised from one sentence about it, which is this project's own standing lesson about reading a thing rather than a note about it.

Kept separate from the interview-reference question because they answer different halves: that one asks what is KEPT, this asks in what ORDER the parse happens. They share a trigger in one option each, which is the relation drawn rather than a reason to merge them.","status":"proposed"}
